newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: IMPORT PRESSURE WEAKENS ZIMBABWE DOLLAR FURTHER.
newsitem.headline: IMPORT PRESSURE WEAKENS ZIMBABWE DOLLAR FURTHER.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar continued straining under import pressure on Thursday with the interbank market at a virtual standstill in the morning as no one was keen to trade, dealers said.
"We had a big import payment yesterday which left the market very dry...about Z$80 million short...no one wants to trade at the moment," one dealer said.
"The central bank poured in a few bucks (U.S. dollars) but that didn't help much," he added.
Dealers however said the current weakeness in the local dollar might encourage exporters to bring foreign funds into the market with an eye to making a hefty profit.

They shrugged off any immediate reaction on the part of the Zimbabwe dollar to a national budget announcement expected later in the day, maintaining that the unit was largely driven by demand and supply.
"We don't expect any surprises in the budget that would move the exchange rates," one dealer said.
At around 0800 GMT the local dollar was trading at 11.4650/4850 to the U.S. dollar compared to late Wednesday's 11.4500/4600 as most banks abandoned the normal one-point bid/offer spread.

Against the crosses, it registered gains on sterling at 19.1590/2040 from 19.2200/2350, tracking a firmer U.S. dollar overseas, but was softer against the mark at 6.2750/2850 compared to 6.2600/2700 and at 2.5140/5200 from 2.4900/5150 against South Africa's rand.
